content.title: How to Scan Documents on iPhone Without an App
content.meta_description: Scan documents on your iPhone or iPad using built-in Notes or Files apps without downloading software. Step-by-step guide to quick PDF scans.
content.h1: How to Scan a Document Without Downloading an App
content.quick_answer: To scan a document without an app, open the iOS Files app, tap the More (...) button, and select Scan Documents. Place your document in view to capture it automatically as a PDF, then save it directly to your chosen folder. Alternatively, use the camera icon inside Apple Notes to scan pages into a note.
intro: When you need to send a signed form or paper document immediately, installing new software or creating an account creates unnecessary delay. Your iPhone and iPad include built-in scanning tools that let you create PDFs right away.

This guide explains how to use the pre-installed Notes and Files apps to capture, save, and share scanned documents without downloading anything from the App Store. It also highlights built-in system limits so you know when a dedicated tool like Document Scanner & PDF Toolkit might be necessary.
content.steps_heading: Step-by-Step: Scan Documents Using the Built-In iOS Files App

steps.title: Open the Files app and start scanning
steps.detail: Open the built-in Files app on your iPhone or iPad. Navigate to the folder where you want to store the document, tap the More (...) button in the upper corner, and select Scan Documents.

steps.title: Frame and capture the paper page
steps.detail: Position your device directly over the paper in good light. The shutter automatically captures the page when borders are clear, or you can tap the shutter button manually if lighting is low.

steps.title: Review pages and save as a PDF
steps.detail: Continue scanning additional pages if your document has multiple sheets. Tap Save when finished; the scan is saved directly into your current folder as a single PDF file.

steps.title: Share or email your PDF
steps.detail: Long-press or tap the newly saved PDF file in the Files app, tap Share, and choose Mail, Messages, or AirDrop to send your document immediately.

content.alternatives_heading: Other Ways to Scan and Process Documents

alternatives.how: Open or create a note in Apple Notes, tap the camera icon, select Scan Documents, scan your pages, and save the note.
alternatives.best_for: Quick scans that you want to keep alongside typed notes or checklists.
alternatives.limitation: Scans are saved inside note files rather than directly into document folders, requiring extra taps to export as standalone PDFs.

alternatives.how: Capture pages with automatic edge detection, apply shadow removal or contrast filters, compress large PDFs, or sign forms before sharing.
alternatives.best_for: Complex documents that require custom PDF compression, precise shadow removal, or form filling.
alternatives.limitation: Exporting to editable Word (.docx) requires a Pro in-app purchase, though core scanning and compression are free.

content.features_heading: Advanced Scanning Tools for Complex Documents

feature_points.benefit: Automatically detects page borders in the camera view and corrects perspective, ensuring clean rectangular scans even when shooting from an angle.
Captures multiple pages in one session and combines them into a single PDF, letting you reorder individual pages before exporting.
Applies one-tap color and black-and-white filters plus shadow removal to clean up uneven lighting or phone shadows that native scanners miss.
Saves scans as PDF or JPG and exports directly to iCloud Drive, Google Drive, Dropbox, or email without uploading files to external processing servers.

content.tips_heading: Tips for Getting Clean Scans with Built-In iOS Tools
tips: Place your document on a high-contrast background, such as dark paper on a light table, to help the built-in scanner detect edges cleanly.
Hold your iPhone directly above the paper under even light to minimize phone shadows, as native iOS tools lack a dedicated shadow-removal filter.
If you need to scan a specialized receipt with faded print or an official passport photo, review our guides on scanning receipts on iPhone or scanning passport photos for specific requirements.
To combine multiple image files into one PDF in Files, select the images, tap More (...), and pick Create PDF; note that page ordering relies on your selection order.

faqs.question: How do you scan documents using the built-in iOS Notes app?
faqs.answer: Open or create a note in the built-in Notes app, then tap the camera or paperclip button and choose Scan Documents. Position your camera over the document to capture it, tap Save, and share the generated PDF directly from the note.

faqs.question: How do you scan directly to a PDF in the iOS Files app?
faqs.answer: Open the Files app, open the folder where you want your file saved, tap the More (...) button, and choose Scan Documents. After capturing your pages, tap Save to generate a single PDF file stored directly in that folder location.

faqs.question: Can built-in iOS scanning tools remove shadows or compress file size?
faqs.answer: The built-in Notes and Files scanners apply basic contrast adjustments, but iOS has no dedicated shadow-removal filter or built-in control for compressing PDFs to a target file size. If your scanned PDF exceeds email file size limits, you will need a tool with compression features.

faqs.question: How do you share or email the PDF generated by Apple Notes or Files?
faqs.answer: In the Files app, tap and hold the PDF file, tap Share, and select Mail or another app. In Apple Notes, tap the scanned document inside the note, tap the Share icon, and choose your preferred destination.

faqs.question: When is it worth downloading a dedicated document scanning app?
faqs.answer: Downloading a dedicated app like Document Scanner & PDF Toolkit is useful when you need to remove stubborn phone shadows, compress large PDF files to meet 20-25 MB email limits, sign forms, or export scans to editable Word documents. For complete app evaluations, see our best free PDF scanner app guide.
